subject: GPU footprint scenarios, min-floor and rolling activation — KestrelTech
body:
From: Evie Long <evie.long@kestreltech.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Capacity planning — quick details we need

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. As discussed, procurement wants a short write-up of the options we can include in the proposal so they can see the cost/availability trade-offs. Top-line asks:

- A min-GPU floor we recommend as the baseline for predictable latency for our conversational agents (we expect ~120 requests/s at 2k tokens).
- A 3-stage ramp schedule (initial pilot, steady growth, projected peak after 6 months).
- A fallback model/quantization option if we hit capacity constraints or need a low-cost tier.

Can you send 2–3 discrete pricing/size options and an indicative onboarding timeline? Procurement also asked if you can include an example warm-up window and a soft-decommit clause (for months 3–6).

Would appreciate a single PDF and a short MOU draft.

Best,
Evie
Evie Long
Head of AI Ops — KestrelTech

---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Evie Long <evie.long@kestreltech.io>
Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU footprint scenarios, min-floor and rolling activation — KestrelTech

Hi Evie —

Thanks, glad the call was useful. I put together 3 options (attached) that map to the pilot → steady → growth stages. High level below, and I cc'd our capacity lead and solutions architect to make sure the technical assumptions line up.

Summary (attached: Kestrel_GPU_Options_v1.pdf):

1) Pilot (Conservative) — 8 GPUs minimum (A100 equivalent), single region
   - Target: ~20 req/s sustained, burst to 60 req/s
   - Ramp: 0–30 days activation window; warm-up credits for first 2 weeks
   - Fallback: quantized model variant (4-bit) saved as alternate route

2) Baseline (Recommended) — 24 GPUs minimum, geo-redundant in 2 regions
   - Target: ~100 req/s sustained, 200 req/s burst
   - Ramp: 30–90 days phased activation, can start 12 GPUs then ramp to 24
   - Soft-decommit window months 3–6: reduce up to 25% with 30 days notice

3) Growth (Aggressive) — 64 GPUs reserved, multi-zone, priority throughput
   - Target: >250 req/s sustained for mixed workloads
   - Ramp: 60–180 days staged activation with burst lanes
   - Includes reserved warm standby for blue/green canary launches

I attached a short MOU draft (MOU-draft-Kestrel.docx) that captures the soft-decommit language and warm-up credit mechanics.

Questions for you (so we lock pricing and SLOs):
- Is the 30–90 day phased activation acceptable for Baseline?
- Do you need per-route token budgets (we can attach route-level cost caps to the SLOs)?
- Any compliance constraints for geo-redundancy (preferred regions)?

Next steps: Jonas will chime in on the activation sequencing and Ben will provide the throughput anchors we used to size the Baseline. If that looks good, I can turn this into a concise proposal PDF and a DocuSign-ready MOU.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales Director
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Evie Long <evie.long@kestreltech.io>
Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: GPU footprint scenarios, min-floor and rolling activation — KestrelTech

Kim / Ben / Evie — quick technical callouts after reviewing the numbers:

- Baseline math: for 2k-token average responses and the 100 req/s sustained target, 24 A100-ish GPUs with continuous batching + KV cache looks right if we:
  * Enable prefix KV caching for hot models (reduces token compute ~30%)
  * Use 2-model-tier routing (full-precision primary, 4-bit fallback)

- Pilot: 8 GPUs is safe for a functional pilot but we should specify that initial latency SLO is 150–250ms p50 for short responses; larger prompts will see tail increases.

- Warm-up: recommend a 10-day warm-up credit (not two weeks) if we accept a short burst window on day 7–10 to pre-populate KV caches. That reduces billable spend while achieving similar latency after warm-up.

- Soft-decommit: operationally we can honor a 25% reduction between months 3–6 with a 45-day notice and a one-time rewarm fee for stateful caches if they decommit below 50% of baseline.

I'll add a short appendix with per-route anchors (tokens/sec -> GPU %) for the PDF.

—Jonas
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: GPU footprint scenarios, min-floor and rolling activation — KestrelTech

Quick numbers to include in the PDF (rounded):

- Pilot (8 GPUs): supports ~18–25 req/s sustained for mixed prompt lengths; estimate monthly token spend $22k–$28k depending on burst.
- Baseline (24 GPUs): supports ~90–120 req/s sustained; token spend range $60k–$80k/month.
- Growth (64 GPUs): supports >260 req/s; token spend $160k+/month.

Notes: pricing assumes standard batching and typical token distribution (70% short replies, 30% long). We should publish a small table showing sensitivity to average prompt length — clients love that.

I'll paste these into the PDF and add a short row for the warm-up credit economics (10-day credit equivalent to ~15% of first-month bill).

—Ben
Capacity Planning Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Subject: Proposal: GPU footprint scenarios & activation cadence (KestrelTech)

Evie — attached is the PDF (Kestrel_GPU_Options_v1.pdf) and a short MOU. Highlights:

- Baseline recommendation: 24 GPUs as the min-floor for predictable latency; phased activation (12 -> 24) over 30–90 days.
- Warm-up: 10-day warm-up credit; we will provide a burst window on day 7 for cache seeding.
- Soft-decommit: up to 25% reduction months 3–6 with 45-day notice; rewarm fee applied if decommit <50% baseline.
- Pricing anchors provided in table (pilot/baseline/growth) with ranges and assumptions.

Attachments: Kestrel_GPU_Options_v1.pdf (proposal), MOU-draft-Kestrel.docx (contract stub).

Next steps: if procurement is good, we can convert MOU -> DocuSign. I can also add per-route token caps if you want explicit budget ceilings.

Best,
Kimberly Park

If those are ok, procurement will move forward and we can book an onboarding kickoff for the week of 4/26.

Evie
